messages.content: Decide only whether the NEXT action demands a hand or foot that the PREVIOUS action explicitly leaves occupied by a different independent task. Return JSON only. Do not invent extra grip capacity, release, retrieval, transfer, or repositioning. Reusing the occupied limb to continue operating the SAME held object/task is NO_CONFLICT. If the text explicitly frees, sets down, pockets, transfers, or repositions the object before the new task, that is NO_CONFLICT. If an occupied limb must perform a different independent task with no explicit freeing/repositioning, return CONFLICT. Ignore all non-limb coherence.

PREVIOUS MICRO-ACTION:
Dax presses the brake pedal with his right foot.

NEXT MICRO-ACTION:
Dax keeps pressing the brake and stomps a separate pedal with the same right foot.

Return {"status":"CONFLICT|NO_CONFLICT"}.

message.reasoning:
We need to decide if next action demands hand or foot that previous action explicitly leaves occupied by different independent task. The previous micro-action: Dax presses the brake pedal with his right foot. So right foot is occupied pressing brake. Next micro-action: Dax keeps pressing the brake and stomps a separate pedal with same right foot. He continues pressing brake (same object) and also stomps another pedal with same right foot. That means he uses same foot for two independent tasks? The second task "stomps a separate pedal" is different from pressing brake. So it's an additional independent task on the same limb without freeing it. Thus conflict.

Return {"status":"CONFLICT"}
